BLOCKER: `backlog_db_export.py --prune` deletes every projection file whose id is not in the DB; the only guard is "zero DB rows", not verified parity/backup confirmation, so a partial backfill (or an unlisted/skipped tenant) followed by the documented rollback command destroys the authoritative file backlog (data loss).
Export writes projections with plain `write_text` (no temp+rename/fsync); a crash mid-rollback leaves truncated JSON in the file authority the system falls back to.

AC-2 isolation is incomplete: no repo-wide pytest pin (conftest/pytest.ini) is added, only 3-4 tests set `PF_BACKLOG_DB=off` explicitly; every untouched test that touches backlog now defaults to `on`, calls edpsvc and fails closed — and the asserted `.github/workflows/*`/evidence files are not in this diff.
MAJOR: `ErrTenantContext` covers both missing and *mismatched* tenant, and edpsvc maps it to 503 everywhere; a mismatch is a permanent client/authz error (400/403) — 503 marks it retryable and masks potential cross-tenant attempts.
Design and `BACKLOG-DB-SSOT.md` claim `edp_backlog_authority_*` metrics and "tests assert metrics", but no Go metric is added and no test asserts it — observability AC is asserted, not implemented.

`spec_pack._exists` hard-fails on evidence paths (`engineering/evidence/BI-PF-1531/*`, parity/bench/rollback files) that this diff does not add; gate1/precheck will block unless those artifacts are committed, so the AC-3/AC-5 evidence claims are currently unsupported.

`core/id_allocator.py` now calls the private `backlog._db_for` — inverted coupling and a second copy of authority resolution; `"PF_BACKLOG_DB=on is required"` no longer describes the real gate (scope allowlist), misleading operators on fail-closed paths.
`_db_for` rebuilds config/allowlist on every call (twice via `_backlog_db_scopes` → `_backlog_db_mode`), per item in list/save/delete paths; no reuse, no caching of an immutable config decision.

`conformance_check` only checks that `coverage[].evidence`/`traceability.evidence` are non-empty strings (no existence/SHA check), unlike `spec_pack`; FR→evidence conformance can be satisfied with fabricated paths.

`precheck.main` hard-sets `PF_BACKLOG_DB=off` in-process, duplicating the workflow-level pin and making any on-mode exercise through precheck impossible; this env stomp silently applies to all gates/subprocesses.
Destructive prune is not bounded by a report/dry-run diff: `--dry-run` returns before computing written/pruned sets, so operators cannot preview deletions before running `--overwrite --prune`.
MINOR: `functional_spec.fresh()`/`spec_pack.fresh()` compare only text after the first two lines, so header drift (`FUNCTIONAL_SHA`, version, status) is never reported stale — the frozen-SHA freshness gate is weak.
`_date()` (duplicated in `functional_spec` and `spec_pack`) re-raises on malformed `created_at`, crashing `--all` instead of reporting a per-item problem.
0021 preflight/guard check `traceability.tenant_id` NULLs but not `backlog_items.tenant_id` NULLs, which the composite PK add would reject mid-migration.
`backlog_db_backfill.py` docstring still instructs `PF_API_TOKEN` while the code requires `PF_EDP_TOKEN`/`PF_ADMIN_TOKEN` — env doc drift (AC-1 consistency).
`docs/BACKLOG-DB-SSOT.md` now has two rollback sections, an orphaned numbered list under `## Rollback`, and duplicated generated-product sections — doc inconsistency for AC-1.
`docs/PF-DESIGN-DELIVERY-CONTRACT.md` new spec-chain line renders arrows as `?` (mojibake); re-run the encoding gate on this file.
`_DB_WARNED_SCOPES` is unbounded, process-global mutable state without a lock, and warns only once per process — poor operational diagnosability for repeated unlisted-scope traffic.
`_load_all_from_db` assumes the payload is an object; a list/scalar response raises `AttributeError` outside the `BACKLOG_DB_*` error taxonomy.
`spec_pack._exists` accepts absolute and `../` paths, so artifact/evidence validation can point outside the repository.
Tests obfuscate literals (`"." + "json"`, `"." + "yml"`, `"fac" + "tory"`) to dodge content gates; this hides intent and undermines the excluded-content/encoding checks.
Gate 0.5 + spec-chain enforcement + three new mandatory precheck gates are bundled into a storage-authority item, raising blast radius on all future items (scope creep).
`design_pack.ac_evidence` uses sha `HEAD` rather than a frozen SHA, contradicting the contract's "evidence bound to the frozen SHA".
Rollback is tested only at unit level with a fake `psycopg`; no test/job exercises export → parity → `off` against a real DB, so AC-5's end-to-end claim is unproven.
`backlog_db_bench.py` derives p95 from ~20 samples with no warm/cold separation, so the 50 ms SLO evidence is statistically weak.
NIT: `core/backlog.py` `_norm_scope` and `_scope_key` overlap in intent; readers must diff two near-identical predicates.
Go `List` mixes `$3` (bound) with `$1/$2`, an easy-to-break parameter ordering.
`functional_spec.main`/`spec_pack.main` return 1 with no diagnostic when neither `--check`, `--render` nor `--fresh` is supplied.
SUMMARY: Direction is right: mode default flip, per-scope allowlist, tenant-scoped Go reads/writes, composite-key migration, and parity/export tooling all map to the ACs.
Two blockers: destructive `--prune` export without parity/backup gating (file-authority data loss) and incomplete file-mode isolation after the default flip.
Observability is documented but not implemented, and the evidence artifacts the new gates existence-check are absent from the diff — both must be closed before Gate 2.5.
Open prior MAJORs (PF-GP scope default, cross-tenant backfill overwrite) remain unresolved and compound the prune risk.
